newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenians go to polls to elect president.
newsitem.headline: Armenians go to polls to elect president.

text.p: Armenians began voting in a presidential election on Sunday in which Levon Ter-Petrosyan is seeking another five years in office but faces a challenge from his former prime minister.
The country's 1,596 polling stations opened at 8 a.m. (0400 GMT) and were due to close at 10 p.m (1800 GMT), the Central Elections Commission said.
The 2.4 million electorate is choosing between four candidates but the main battle is between Ter-Petrosyan and former prime minister Vazgen Manukyan.
Ter-Petrosyan, 50, has dominated Armenia's political landscape since it won independence from the Soviet Union in 1991.
Manukyan, also 50, is a former close associate who has promised to raise living standards quickly in the impoverished Caucasus state.
If no candidate gains a majority in Sunday's voting, a second round runoff will be held in two weeks.
While many independent analysts predict a Ter-Petrosyan victory in the first round, they say a high turnout could be good news for Manukyan.
Several dozen international observers are monitoring the voting.
